q: How long is a regulation NBA basketball court?
hint: For scale: a city bus is about {12 m} long.

q: How high above the floor is an Olympic gymnastics balance beam?
hint: For scale: a standard door is about {2 m} tall.

q: How wide is the ring a sumo wrestler must stay inside?
hint: For scale: a king-size bed is about {2 m} long.
clue: A typical parking space is about {5.5 m} long.
card: Before bouts, wrestlers toss salt onto the raised clay ring to purify it.

q: How long is an Olympic rowing race?
hint: For scale: an Olympic running track is {400 m} around.
clue: The swim in a full Ironman triathlon is about {3.9 km}.

q: How long is one lap of the Monaco Grand Prix circuit?
hint: For scale: a marathon is about {42 km}.

q: In what year was the first Rugby World Cup played?

q: In what year was the Stanley Cup first awarded?
hint: For scale: the American Civil War ended in 1865.

q: How many episodes of Lost were made?
hint: For scale: a typical US network drama season has about 22 episodes.
clue: Breaking Bad ran for 62 episodes.
card: Its six seasons aired on ABC from 2004 to 2010.

q: How many episodes of Mad Men were made?
hint: For scale: a typical cable drama season has about 13 episodes.
clue: Game of Thrones ran for 73 episodes.
card: Its seven seasons follow ad man Don Draper through the 1960s.

q: How long is The Dark Knight (2008), in minutes?
hint: For scale: most feature films run 90 to 120 minutes.

q: How long is The Matrix (1999), in minutes?
hint: For scale: Disney’s The Lion King (1994) runs 88 minutes.
clue: The original Star Wars (1977) runs 121 minutes.
card: Its slow-motion “bullet time” effect came from a row of still cameras fired in rapid succession.

q: In what year was Quentin Tarantino’s Pulp Fiction released?
hint: For scale: Jaws came out in 1975.
clue: Back to the Future came out in 1985.

q: How many Oscars did Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022) win?
hint: For scale: Titanic won 11 Oscars.
clue: Slumdog Millionaire won 8.

q: How many seasons of the TV drama Downton Abbey were made?
hint: For scale: the US version of The Office ran for 9 seasons.
clue: Breaking Bad ran for 5 seasons.
card: Highclere Castle in Hampshire, England, stood in for the Crawley family’s home.

q: In what year did Michael Jackson release the album Thriller?
hint: For scale: the Beatles broke up in 1970.
clue: Nirvana released Nevermind in 1991.
card: It is widely reported to be the best-selling album of all time.

q: How long is Bob Dylan’s “Like a Rolling Stone,” in seconds?
hint: For scale: most pop singles run about three to four minutes.
clue: The Beatles’ “Hey Jude” runs about 431 seconds.
card: Rolling Stone magazine ranked it the greatest song of all time in 2004.

q: How many weeks did “Despacito” spend at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100?
hint: For scale: most No. 1 hits stay on top for only a few weeks.
clue: Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” spent 14 weeks at No. 1.

q: How many shows did Ed Sheeran play on his ÷ (Divide) Tour?
hint: For scale: a typical arena tour plays about 50 shows.
clue: Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour had 149 shows.
card: When it ended in 2019, it was the highest-grossing concert tour of all time.

q: In what year did the music-sharing service Napster launch?
hint: For scale: the first music CDs went on sale in 1982.
clue: Spotify launched in 2008.
card: It was started by college student Shawn Fanning and was shut down after record labels sued.

q: How old was Stevie Wonder when his single “Fingertips” hit No. 1 in the US?
hint: For scale: in the US you can vote at 18.
clue: Michael Jackson was 11 when the Jackson 5 first hit No. 1.
card: It came from a live album titled Recorded Live: The 12 Year Old Genius.

q: In what year did Elvis Presley die?
hint: For scale: Elvis released “Heartbreak Hotel” in 1956.
clue: The Beatles broke up in 1970.
card: Graceland, his home in Memphis, opened to the public as a museum in 1982.

q: How many properties can be bought in a standard game of Monopoly, railroads and utilities included?
hint: For scale: a standard deck has 52 playing cards.
clue: A Monopoly board has 40 spaces around its edge.
card: The street names on the original US board come from Atlantic City, New Jersey.

q: How many cards are in a standard Pokémon Trading Card Game deck?
hint: For scale: Uno players are each dealt 7 cards to start.
clue: A standard deck of playing cards has 52 cards.
card: Players take the role of Pokémon Trainers, sending their cards’ creatures into battle.

q: How many holes are on a standard Chinese checkers board?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 64 squares.
clue: A Sudoku grid has 81 small squares.
card: Despite the name, the game was invented in Germany in 1892 as “Stern-Halma.”

q: How many colored wedges must you collect to fill your pie in classic Trivial Pursuit?
hint: For scale: a Twister mat has 24 colored circles.
clue: Uno cards come in 4 colors.
card: It was invented in 1979 by two Canadian journalists who found pieces missing from their Scrabble set.

q: In what year did Sony release the first PlayStation in Japan?
hint: For scale: Pac-Man came out in 1980.
clue: Nintendo released the first Game Boy in 1989.
card: Sony built it after a deal to make a CD drive for Nintendo fell apart.

q: In what year did Wikipedia launch?
hint: For scale: the World Wide Web became public in 1991.
clue: Amazon was founded in 1994.
card: It began as a side project to Nupedia, an encyclopedia written only by experts.

q: How many dice are rolled in a game of Yahtzee?
hint: For scale: Monopoly is played with 2 dice.
clue: A standard die has 6 faces.
card: Players get up to three rolls per turn, choosing which dice to keep each time.

q: How tall is the Little Mermaid statue in Copenhagen?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty is {93 m} tall to the torch.
clue: An average adult man is about {1.75 m} tall.
card: It was unveiled in 1913, inspired by Hans Christian Andersen’s fairy tale.

q: How tall is the Sphere, the giant LED-covered venue in Las Vegas?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
clue: The London Eye is {135 m} tall.
card: It opened in 2023 with a run of concerts by U2.

q: How long is London’s Tower Bridge, end to end?
hint: For scale: a soccer pitch is about {105 m} long.
clue: The Eiffel Tower is {330 m} tall.
card: Its roadway splits in the middle and lifts to let tall ships pass underneath.

q: In what year did construction of the Leaning Tower of Pisa begin?
hint: For scale: the Magna Carta was sealed in 1215.
clue: Work on Notre-Dame de Paris began in 1163.
card: It started to lean once building reached the second floor, because the ground beneath was soft.

q: In what year was the Hoover Dam completed?
hint: For scale: the Panama Canal opened in 1914.
clue: The Empire State Building opened in 1931.
card: It was handed over to the federal government more than two years ahead of schedule.

q: How many steps make up the Spanish Steps in Rome?
hint: For scale: a flight of stairs between two floors of a house has about 13 steps.
clue: The Empire State Building has 102 floors.
card: The stairway climbs from the Piazza di Spagna up to the Trinità dei Monti church at the top.

q: How tall is Michelangelo’s statue of David, not counting its base?
hint: For scale: a basketball hoop’s rim is {3.05 m} high.
clue: A London double-decker bus is about {4.4 m} tall.
card: Its marble block lay neglected in a Florence workshop yard for about 25 years before Michelangelo took it on.

q: How many hours long is a day on Mars?
hint: For scale: a day on Jupiter lasts under 10 hours.
clue: A day on Neptune lasts about 16 hours.
card: Scientists call a Martian day a “sol,” and rover teams have lived on Mars time, shifting their days later and later.

q: What is the diameter of Uranus?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {12,742 km} across.
clue: Saturn is about {120,536 km} across.
card: Uranus spins on its side, so each pole spends decades facing the Sun.

q: How hot can the daytime surface of Mercury get?
hint: For scale: water boils at {100 °C}.
clue: Lead melts at {327 °C}.
card: Venus is hotter still, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun, because Venus’s thick air traps heat.

q: In what year did the first crew move in to live aboard the International Space Station?
hint: For scale: Mir’s first module was launched in 1986.
clue: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990.
card: People have lived aboard it without a break ever since, the longest continuous human presence in space.

q: How many hours did Apollo 11’s lunar module Eagle spend on the Moon’s surface?
hint: For scale: Armstrong and Aldrin spent about two and a half hours walking outside.
clue: An Earth day is 24 hours long.
card: Before lifting off, the crew left a plaque reading “We came in peace for all mankind.”

q: In what year was the famous Earthrise photo taken from lunar orbit?
hint: For scale: Sputnik 1 was launched in 1957.
clue: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space in 1961.
card: Apollo 8 astronaut Bill Anders took it on Christmas Eve, during the first crewed trip around the Moon.

q: How far is Saturn from the Sun, on average?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {150,000,000 km} from the Sun.
clue: Jupiter is about {778,500,000 km} from the Sun.
card: Saturn is less dense than water, so in a big enough bathtub it would float.

q: How many arms does a squid have, not counting its two long tentacles?
hint: For scale: a starfish typically has 5 arms.
clue: A lobster has 10 legs.
card: Like octopuses, squid have three hearts and blue blood.

q: How many teeth does an adult pig have?
hint: For scale: a child’s full set of milk teeth is 20.
clue: An adult human has 32 teeth, wisdom teeth included.
card: A boar’s tusks are really overgrown canine teeth that keep growing all its life.

q: In what year did Jane Goodall begin studying wild chimpanzees at Gombe in Tanzania?
hint: For scale: Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859.
clue: The double-helix structure of DNA was published in 1953.
card: She watched a chimp poke grass stalks into a termite mound to fish out termites, showing that animals use tools.

q: How many species of rhinoceros are alive today?
hint: For scale: humans are the only living species in the genus Homo.
clue: There are 3 living species of elephant.
card: Rhino horns are made of keratin, the same material as human fingernails.

q: How fast can an emu sprint?
hint: For scale: a typical person jogs at about {10 km/h}.
clue: An ostrich can run at about {70 km/h}.
card: Like ostriches, emus cannot fly and rely on their long, powerful legs instead.

q: In what year did Louis Pasteur first give his rabies vaccine to a person?
hint: For scale: Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859.
clue: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876.
card: His first patient was a nine-year-old boy bitten by a rabid dog, and the boy survived.

q: How many basic tastes do scientists widely recognize?
hint: For scale: a rainbow is traditionally said to have 7 colors.
clue: The human heart has 4 chambers.
card: Umami, the savory taste of broths and parmesan, was named by Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda in 1908.

q: How many lifeboats did the Titanic carry?
hint: For scale: the Titanic had 4 funnels.
clue: The Titanic’s hull was split into 16 watertight compartments.
card: Together they could hold about 1,178 people, roughly half of those on board.

q: How heavy is Big Ben, the great bell inside London’s Elizabeth Tower?
hint: For scale: a large car weighs about {2 t}.
clue: An adult male African elephant weighs about {6 t}.
card: It cracked within months of being installed in 1859, which is why it rings slightly off-key.

q: In what year did Benjamin Franklin carry out his famous kite experiment?
hint: For scale: the US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
clue: Captain Cook reached the east coast of Australia in 1770.
card: He used a key tied to the kite string to show that lightning is electricity.

q: How many days did it take to build the Empire State Building?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower took a little over two years to build.
clue: A year has 365 days.
card: It was structurally finished twelve days ahead of schedule.

q: How many ships sailed with Christopher Columbus on his first voyage in 1492?
hint: For scale: the Pilgrims crossed the Atlantic in a single ship, the Mayflower.
clue: Ferdinand Magellan set out with 5 ships in 1519.
card: The Santa María ran aground on Christmas Day 1492 and never sailed home.

q: In what year did London’s Great Exhibition open in the Crystal Palace?
hint: For scale: Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
clue: The American Civil War ended in 1865.
card: The Crystal Palace was a giant iron-and-glass hall put up in Hyde Park in under a year.

q: How old was Alexander the Great when he died?
hint: For scale: Queen Victoria reigned for 63 years.
clue: Julius Caesar was 55 when he died.
card: By then his empire stretched from Greece to the edge of India.

q: How long is a Boeing 737-800, one of the most common airliners?

card: More than 7,000 planes of the 737 Next Generation family, which includes the -800, were delivered.

q: What was Concorde’s top speed?

clue: Sound travels at about {1,235 km/h} at sea level.
card: Flying west, it could land in New York earlier, by the clock, than it had left London.

q: How much did ENIAC, the famous 1940s electronic computer, weigh?
hint: For scale: an African elephant weighs about {6 t}.
clue: A fully loaded semi truck can weigh about {36 t}.
card: It filled a room with about 18,000 vacuum tubes.

q: How much did NASA’s Ingenuity helicopter, which flew on Mars, weigh?
hint: For scale: a heavy bowling ball weighs {7.26 kg}.
clue: A typical laptop weighs about {1.4 kg}.
card: In 2021 it made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.

q: What was the wingspan of the Wright brothers’ 1903 Flyer?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 747’s wingspan is about {68 m}.
clue: A tennis court is about {24 m} long.
card: The original Flyer now hangs in the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum in Washington.

q: In what year did the first Toyota Corolla go on sale?
hint: For scale: Ford started selling the Model T in 1908.
clue: Honda launched the first Civic in 1972.
card: It went on to become the best-selling car nameplate in history.

q: How much did the original 2010 Wi-Fi iPad weigh?
hint: For scale: the original 2007 iPhone weighed about {0.135 kg}.
clue: A regulation soccer ball weighs about {0.43 kg}.
card: Apple sold about 300,000 on its first day in the US.

q: How tall is Victoria Falls on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border?

clue: The Statue of Liberty is {93 m} tall to the torch.
card: Locals call it Mosi-oa-Tunya, “the smoke that thunders,” for its spray visible from far away.

q: What is the surface area of Lake Victoria, Africa’s largest lake?
hint: For scale: Lake Baikal covers about {31,700 sq km}.
clue: Lake Superior covers about {82,100 sq km}.
card: It is one of the main sources of the Nile.

q: How much soda does a standard US can hold?
hint: For scale: a large bottle of soda holds {2 L}.
clue: A standard wine bottle holds {0.75 L}.
card: That size became the US standard in the 1980s and 1990s, as cans switched from steel to aluminum.

q: How many US states share a land border with Mexico?

q: How many ridges are on the edge of a US dime?
